text:
incident-bot: [P1] ALERT: Multiple nodes in inference-pool-1 moved to NotReady (kubelet restart). Observed cascade: a handful of runtime containers OOM/killed with CUDA errors, traffic retries increasing. Paging @eng-oncall.

alex: I'm on it. seeing spikes in 95p latency and a bunch of `OOMKilled` + `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` in the runtime pods.

priya: confirmed. kubectl on cluster-prod: `kubectl get nodes --selector=pool=inference-pool-1 -o wide` shows 3/8 NotReady.

sam: grabbing logs now. sample from node ip-10-12-5-34: 
```
(kernel) Out of memory: Kill process 31415 (redwood-runtime) score 120 or sacrifice child
E Cuda error: unspecified launch failure
containerd: container exited with status 137
```

maya: can we cordon the NotReady nodes so pods don't come back to them during restart?

alex: yes, cordon + drain if they're flapping. doing `kubectl cordon ip-10-12-5-34` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force ip-10-12-5-34` for the obvious culprits.

dmitri: infra looking at kubelet logs and dmesg for OOM reasons. early signal that GPU memory driver on 5-34 hit a kernel GPU reset. Trying `systemctl restart kubelet` on the node as well — but if it immediately flips to NotReady we should isolate.

priya: routing policy update: temporarily route traffic away from inference-pool-1 to inference-pool-2 (warm spare) and to dedicated-capacity fallback. Updating routing weights in control-plane now.

alex: applied temporary policy: inference-pool-1 weight -> 0.3, pool-2 -> 0.6, dedicated-fallback -> 0.1. Will monitor error rates.

sam: also pushing a hotfix: reduce default batch size from 8 to 2 in runtime config for pool-2 to reduce memory pressure. Patch applied via configmap update: 
```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/runtime BATCH_MAX=2
```

incident-bot: NOTE: Customer-impact tag set. Affected: customers using real-time endpoints on inference-pool-1. ETA for next update in 10m.

maya: I've started a short page to SRE infra team: `@dmitri` you're on infra — any chance of kernel-level regression?

dmitri: digging. so far kernel GPU driver v520.x shows a reported bug, but we need full node dumps. I've requested a hot node-sysdump from support-agent. If nodes restart cleanly and remain Ready for >5m we'll start re-introducing traffic.

priya: notifying account teams for any customers with high error rates >5% in the last 15m. Preparing a brief to post to #incidents and #customer-success.

alex: handoff note for next on-call (if I'm paged out): current mitigations: nodes cordoned/drained, traffic routed away, batch size reduced, kernel restart attempts in progress. Monitor: errors (OOMKilled, CUDA errors), 95/99 latency, queue length, and the node Ready count.

sam: quick reminder — enable autoscaler temporary surge: `kubectl scale --replicas=20 deployment/runtime` in pool-2 to absorb traffic while we recover. Doing now.

dmitri: infra-bot: node-snapshot uploaded for ip-10-12-5-34 to s3://redwood-dumps/1795002468/34.tar.gz. Will start kernel driver rollback if the dumps confirm regression.

incident-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: cordon/drain x3 nodes; routing weight changed; batch size reduced; scale up executed; node-snapshot uploaded. Next update +20m or on significant state change.

maya: posting initial customer bulletin draft to #incidents for review. keep text simple: brief impact, mitigations, ETA for updates.

alex: if nodes come back Ready, we'll uncordon one-by-one and carefully reintroduce traffic to avoid triggering OOMs. plan: reintroduce 10% at a time with canary requests.

priya: thanks all, I'll coordinate CS notifications and keep the incident page updated.

sam: logging a postmortem ticket with initial timeline and logs. tagging for follow-up: kernel driver, runtime memory handling, autoscaler tuning.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: at 1795002922, 2 nodes still NotReady, traffic routing stable to pool-2/dedicated, error rate decreased from 7.8% -> 1.1%. Continuing monitoring.
